# Mixed-language integration fixture

Each project includes an index generated by the corresponding real SCIP indexer. Tests replay those indexes with the checked-in source, so they can run on Windows without native compilers or Docker. Only the SCIP metadata's project root and tool argument list were normalized for portability.

| Project | Reproduction |
|---|---|
| `python` | Run scip-python 0.6.8 on Linux with Node 20 using `scip-python index . --project-name=cockpit-fixture --environment=environment.json --output=index.scip`. |
| `go` | Run scip-go 0.2.9 with Go 1.27.1 using `scip-go index --module-root=. --repository-remote=example.com/cockpit-fixture --module-version=fixture --skip-tests --output=index.scip ./...`. This index was produced on Windows. |
| `java` | Mount the project at `/src`. Compile the two sources with JDK 21 and SemanticDB javac 0.12.3 on the compiler classpath. Pass `-Xplugin:semanticdb -sourceroot:/src -targetroot:/tmp/classes` as a single argument and set `-d /tmp/classes`. Run `scip-java index-semanticdb --output=/src/index.scip /tmp/classes` with scip-java 0.12.3 from `/src`. |
| `native` | Mount the project at `/src` in Linux x64 with GCC and G++ for the supplied compilation database. From `/src`, run scip-clang 0.4.1 using `scip-clang --jobs 1 --index-output-path index.scip --show-compiler-diagnostics`. |

The Python fixture covers a relative import and two calls to the imported alias after a non-BMP character. The Go fixture exercises package imports and interface dispatch. The Java fixture exercises cross-package inheritance and overloaded methods. The C fixture exercises a header declaration, cross-file and recursive calls, and a function pointer. The C++ fixture exercises namespaced overloads, a template, and virtual dispatch.

To run the optional Docker lifecycle test, build an image with the Dockerfile below, set `COCKPIT_TEST_INDEXER_IMAGE` to its full SHA-256 image ID, and run `npm -w server test`. This image tests transport and cleanup using the real Go fixture index. Language correctness is tested separately against the original indexer outputs.

```dockerfile
FROM node:20-slim
ENTRYPOINT ["/bin/sh","-ec","case $(cat /workspace/mode 2>/dev/null || true) in failure) exit 7;; sleep) exec sleep 100;; esac; cat /workspace/fixture.scip","cockpit-test"]
```
